title: Getting to Know You
summary: Getting to know each other, checking your level, and the first set of words from a reading text.

title: My Free Time & Hobbies
summary: Hobby vocabulary, play/go/do, adverbs of frequency and four tenses: Present Simple, Present Continuous, Past Simple, Past Continuous. Plus a video and speaking practice.

title: A Day in My Life
titleUk: Daily routine and the two present tenses
summary: Daily routine vocabulary, telling the time, at/on/in, and the main contrast of the lesson: Present Simple vs Present Continuous. Plus state verbs, a reading text and a video.

title: The Day It All Went Wrong
summary: Storytelling vocabulary, Past Simple (regular, irregular, questions), the -ed sounds, Past Continuous and the while/when contrast. With picture tasks, a story to read and a video. Also revises everything from Lessons 2 and 3.

title: Have You Ever…?
summary: Two warm-ups on Lessons 1–4, then life experiences: the third form of verbs, Present Perfect with ever / never, been vs gone, and the key contrast with the Past Simple. With a reading, a video and a 'Have you ever…?' interview.

title: Better, Faster, the Best
summary: A full review of the five tenses we know — Present Simple and Continuous, Past Simple and Continuous, Present Perfect — and a new topic: comparatives and superlatives. With a drag-and-drop vocabulary warm-up, a video, a reading and speaking.

title: Who Is the Greatest?
titleUk: as … as · not as … as · футбол
summary: Football week. as … as and not as … as, with just / nearly / not nearly / twice, as many / as much, the same … as and adjective vs adverb (as well as). A B1 reading about the GOAT debate — Messi, Ronaldo, Pelé, Shevchenko — with whereas / although / despite, a football debate, and the exercises we didn't finish in Lesson 6.
topics: just / nearly / not nearly / twice as … as
as many / as much · the same as
as good as vs as well as

title: Take Up, Take After, Take Over
titleUk: Фразові дієслова і дієслова з прийменниками
summary: 32 verbs that come with a partner word: take up / after / to / off / over, look after / for / up / up to / forward to, get on with / over / into / back, and verbs with fixed prepositions (depend on, rely on, agree with…). Preposition + -ing. A review of all the grammar so far, a reading about what makes a good young player, and three extra exercises.

title: The Press Conference
summary: A speaking lesson. Warm-ups on the verbs with prepositions from Lesson 8 and on question word order. A post-match press conference to read, interview phrases, writing the journalist's questions, then role-plays: player and journalist, interview the teacher, the hot seat. Homework: sentences of your own with verbs + prepositions.
topics: Question word order in five tenses
Preposition at the end of a question
